title: Graceful degradation: load shedding + tighter timeouts + model-variant fallback in degraded regions
author: Elena Popov
release_notes: Adds feature-flagged graceful degradation behaviors for region health=DEGRADED: tier-aware load shedding, tightened upstream timeouts, and policy-based fallback to compatible model variants. Includes metrics to attribute impact and validate SLO burn-rate changes during controlled tests.
body: Context: For regional impairments that aren’t “hard down” (e.g., packet loss, elevated p99, intermittent 5xx), we currently oscillate between doing nothing and initiating full failover. That gap has led to prolonged tail latency + retries, amplification on already-sick clusters, and customer-visible timeouts (see SUP-19312 + incident threads linked from ENG-2852). This PR adds graceful degradation controls that kick in when a region is marked DEGRADED (not FAILED) by the health aggregator/trigger engine, with guardrails to avoid flappiness and to protect higher tiers. Summary of changes (feature flagged): 1) Tier-aware admission control (load shedding): When region_health=DEGRADED, apply a per-route policy that caps in-flight requests and shed new requests above the cap with a deterministic response. Defaults: Enterprise/dedicated tiers are protected (higher cap, lower shed probability). Self-serve/lowest tier sheds first. Shedding response: HTTP 503 with Retry-After: 1 and an internal error code `region_degraded_shed` so clients can classify/retry appropriately. 2) Tightened upstream timeouts (reduce “hung” work): In DEGRADED state we lower upstream timeouts for gateway->runtime and runtime->model-worker calls (request header streaming included) to reduce queue buildup and tail amplification. This is policy driven: separate knobs for `connect_timeout_ms`, `headers_timeout_ms`, `overall_timeout_ms`, and streaming idle timeout. 3) Fallback model variant selection (keep region available without full failover): If a request’s selected model is in a degraded pool OR queue depth crosses the degradation threshold, routing can fall back to a compatible variant (same interface + tokenizer contract) based on an allowlist graph. Examples: - `llama-3.1-70b` -> `llama-3.1-8b` (same family) - `mistral-large` -> `mistral-medium` (where configured) Fallback is only applied when: (a) region_health=DEGRADED, (b) request is eligible per policy (tier/route/model), (c) the target variant is “green” in the same region and passes the existing compatibility check, and (d) the request does not set `x-redwood-no-fallback: true`. Note: This PR does not implement cross-region fallback; that remains under the orchestrator’s progressive failover path (ENG-2846/ENG-2848). Configuration: - New config file `config/degradation_policies.yaml` (loaded by routing service) with per-route knobs: `max_inflight`, `shed_strategy` (hard cap vs probabilistic), timeout overrides, and fallback candidates with priority ordering. - Feature flag: `routing.graceful_degradation_controls` (default OFF everywhere). - “Monitor-only” mode: `routing.graceful_degradation_dry_run` emits metrics for what would have happened without enforcing. Observability: - New counters/gauges: `routing_degradation_state{region}`, `routing_shed_total{region,route,tier,reason}`, `routing_timeout_override_applied_total{region,route}`, `routing_variant_fallback_total{from_model,to_model,route,tier,reason}`, and `routing_degradation_policy_eval_errors_total`. - Structured log event `degradation_decision` (sampled) includes policy version hash, evaluated inputs (tier/route/model), and action taken. - Tracing: adds span attributes `redwood.degradation_state`, `redwood.shed=true/false`, `redwood.fallback_model`. Implementation notes: - Adds `DegradationController` in routing layer that consumes `RegionHealthSnapshot` and `CapacitySignals` (existing) to compute an action plan per request. - Uses existing model compatibility registry; no new model metadata system introduced here. - Ensures hold-down semantics are respected by using the health snapshot’s debounced state (we do not re-debounce locally). Testing: - Unit tests for policy evaluation matrix (tier/route/model eligibility) including “no fallback” header and dry-run behavior. - Integration tests: simulated DEGRADED health snapshot + elevated queue depth, verifying: (a) shed response code + headers, (b) tightened timeouts applied to upstream call, (c) fallback selection picks highest-priority green variant, (d) enterprise tier protected. - Added a small replay harness for routing decisions using captured request descriptors (sanitized) from staging. Rollout plan: - Land behind flags with defaults OFF. - Enable in staging in dry-run mode for 48h, confirm metrics match expected decision rates. - Run in staging enforced mode during the next controlled impairment scenario (perf-canary scenario aligns with PR #267). - For prod: start with a single low-risk route + self-serve tier only, dry-run for 24h, then enforce with on-call approval; monitor SLO burn-rate and shed rate. Risk/mitigations: - Quality impact due to fallback: limited to allowlisted compatible variants; customers can opt out via header; we emit explicit fallback metrics to quantify. - Flappiness: we rely on debounced DEGRADED state from health aggregator; no per-request “local” thresholding beyond queue depth guardrails. - Over-shedding: policy defaults conservative; enterprise tiers protected; dry-run provides calibration before enforcement. Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Wire policy versions + current state into failover audit UI (tracked in ENG-2847). - Evaluate making fallback eligibility an explicit customer-configurable account setting (PM-612 discussion). - Add client-side SDK guidance for Retry-After behavior during controlled tests (docs PR tracked separately).

review_conversation: Mina Haddad: Can we ensure fallback never crosses tokenizer contracts? We’ve been burned by subtle tokenization mismatches before.

Elena Popov: Yes—fallback selection calls the existing compatibility registry (tokenizer + chat template + tool-calling capability gates). I added a test case that rejects a candidate when tokenizer_contract differs.
Aisha Bello: For SLO reporting, we need to distinguish shed vs upstream error vs fallback. Do we have distinct error codes/metrics?
Elena Popov: Added `region_degraded_shed` code, `routing_shed_total`, and `routing_variant_fallback_total`. Also added trace attrs so we can slice latency by action taken.
Peter Holtz: Timeout reductions during DEGRADED could increase 499/408 rates if set too aggressively. Can we gate this separately from shedding/fallback?

Elena Popov: Split flags: `routing.graceful_degradation_controls` enables the controller; within policy, each action can be disabled (timeouts/shedding/fallback). Also added dry-run mode to calibrate before enforcement.
Vikram Singh: Any risk that shed responses amplify retries and worsen load?

Elena Popov: We set Retry-After=1 and shed preferentially for low tier. Also the cap is on in-flight, so we’re preventing queue growth; we can tune via policy once we see client retry behavior in staging.
Sergio Costa: Please add a dashboard-friendly metric name for current degradation state per region.
Elena Popov: Added `routing_degradation_state{region}` gauge with enum mapping in docs comment; will wire into dashboard spec in observability-pack PR.
